clue.text: Goes over bills in America

definitions.meaning: to go over something is to examine or inspect it
in the US a restaurant bill is called a check, so several bills are this plural

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises invoices during a stay in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspects is the verb sense, and US English uses the word for restaurant tabs where British English says bill.

clue.text: Go in with a student of the digestive system

parts.note: to go in is to enter
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car, so a student

explanation.surface: An instruction to enter alongside a trainee gastroenterologist.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner (from the red L-plate on British learner cars) stands for any student in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the intestines, as in feeding by tube into the gut.

clue.text: A way in after support spread

indicators.note: the clue places the A and the way in after the support, so they follow it in the answer

parts.note: a prop is a support
a gate is an entrance or way in

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gap opened up behind a supporting post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is a verb here, as in spreading news or plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To disseminate or make something multiply is to spread it, the verb sense used of ideas and plants.

clue.text: Footballers welcome ties being off for a party

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the footballers' letters receive the rest inside them

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the body governing English football

indicators.note: ties that are off are disordered, so the letters of ties are rearranged

explanation.surface: Footballers are glad to be rid of the neckties before a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: FA is the Football Association, which runs English football; 'ties' looks like neckwear or matches, but it is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style festival or celebration is a kind of party.

clue.text: Does one shoot, having arrived with gunners?

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone shoots, now that the artillery has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the standard crossword gunners. The shooting is photography, not firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers and film crews shoot pictures with this device.

clue.text: One weeps about nothing winning while one rakes it in!

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the others

parts.note: a crier is one who weeps
O is the figure zero, nothing
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A tearful loser makes way for whoever is profiting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: a casino employee rakes in the chips with a long stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino dealer at a roulette table gathers the stakes with a rake.

clue.text: A dressing down for the military

definitions.text: A dressing down for the military

parts.words: A dressing down for the military
parts.note: a dressing down sounds like a scolding, but here it is dressing down in the sense of plain clothes that soldiers wear off duty

explanation.surface: Soldiers receive a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means civilian clothing worn by someone who normally wears uniform.

clue.text: Demote soldiers in front of emissary

indicators.note: the soldiers come first, in front of the emissary, in the answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a legate is an envoy or emissary, especially of the Pope

explanation.surface: An order to downgrade troops who march ahead of a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword way to say soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move down to a lower rank or division, as a football team is.

clue.text: Rant against worker wanting safety feature

indicators.note: against means beside, so the worker is set next to the rant

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to rail is to complain angrily, to rant

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a labourer who lacks protection on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rant against' reads as one phrase, but 'against' is only the juxtaposition signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar to hold on stairs or a balcony protects people from falling.

clue.text: Polish going topless during fish course at dinner!

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: losing the top drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: A Polish diner disrobes partway through the fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, with its capital letter hiding the verb meaning to shine; 'going topless' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A light baked dish of beaten egg whites is served as a starter or dessert.

clue.text: Underpriced hat worn by male

indicators.note: a hat worn by a man goes around him, so the hat's letters surround the male

parts.note: a cap is a hat
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A bargain hat on a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going for less than its worth is low-cost.

clue.text: Catching the last of criminals' accessories

parts.note: trapping means catching

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Seizing what a criminal gang carried with them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means outward decorations and accompaniments, the trimmings that go with something.

clue.text: Most of the journey is free

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: Most of the trip costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something of an unwanted thing is to free it of that thing.

clue.text: City that used to impress

definitions.meaning: the largest city in China, a major port
to impress in the old naval sense is to force into service, which this verb once meant: drugging sailors and carrying them to sea

explanation.surface: A city that once made a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' is not about dazzling: it is the press gang's word for forcing men into the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese port gave its name to the old practice of kidnapping men as crew.

clue.text: Put back iron, fair worn-out!

indicators.note: putting something back turns the word round, read from right to left

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fete is a fair or gala

explanation.surface: Someone returns the iron to its place at an exhausting fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means weak and exhausted, lacking vigour, as worn-out things are.

clue.text: Panics and takes four away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters wander off, so the letters of takes four are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone panics and steals a quartet.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose control in fear or alarm is to panic, a slang phrasal verb.

clue.text: Pilots like them to chase victory over Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the victory comes before the country

parts.note: to tail is to follow or chase
a win is a victory
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Wartime pilots savour pursuing triumph over Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dogfight, but the pilots simply prefer helpful breezes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind blowing from behind speeds an aircraft and saves fuel, so aviators welcome it.

clue.text: Duty changes of course, according to report

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: tacks are a sailing boat's changes of direction into the wind

explanation.surface: A levy shifts direction, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: In sailing, a tack is a turn that changes course.
explanation.definitionFit: A government levy on goods or income is a duty.

clue.text: Weapon that might cause a grave mob riot?

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters of mob are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: A weapon that could lead an angry crowd to disturb a burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crowd disturbing a burial place; the riot is only an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear explosive device dropped from an aircraft is a weapon.

clue.text: Make a mistake giving rights to fourth in line

indicators.note: the fourth letter in the word line is picked out

parts.note: R stands for right, so rights is two of them

explanation.surface: An error that grants entitlements to whoever is fourth in the queue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wrong or blunder is to make a mistake.

clue.text: Young high flier becomes legate abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of legate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A papal envoy becomes a rising star overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The chick of a large bird of prey that soars at height is a youngster in the air.

clue.text: Rise that's 75% Conservative

indicators.note: keeping 75% of a four-letter word means its first three letters stay and the last goes

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political upswing that is mostly Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: a rocky hill rising from moorland, in the West Country of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky hill or high outcrop is a rise in the ground.

clue.text: Wept heartily — is poem one of a series?

indicators.note: heartily means taking the heart, the middle letters of the word

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed with feeling at a verse, wondering if it was one instalment.
explanation.definitionFit: A single instalment of a TV serial is one part of a series.

clue.text: The gall to poke a pal playfully

indicators.note: doing it playfully mixes things around, so the letters of poke a pal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has the nerve to prod a friend in fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gall' suggests cheek, but it is the botanical sense: a growth on an oak caused by a wasp.
explanation.definitionFit: A round growth that forms on oak twigs where a wasp lays its eggs is a plant gall.

clue.text: Indication given to a head of state for delegate

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a sign is an indication

explanation.surface: A signal passed to a president about handing over duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand a task or role to someone else is to delegate it.

clue.text: Food item causing European community retreat?

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: A pastry blamed for causing Europe to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry finger filled with cream is a sweet treat.

clue.text: People with much experience of antique chronometers

parts.note: old means antique
timers are timepieces, chronometers

explanation.surface: Veterans who know about vintage clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterans of long standing are people who have been around for years.

clue.text: String trio start on chardonnay perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first letter comes before the drink
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: chardonnay is an example of white wine

explanation.surface: A string trio begins on the white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'String trio' reads as one musical group, but 'String' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong thread or cord of twisted strands is a kind of string.

clue.text: The fibre in cereals is a laugh!

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone jokes that the roughage in breakfast cereal is comical.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant fibre from an agave leaf is used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Trouble coming up — single lad has an affair

indicators.note: coming up suggests rising back the way it came, so the word for trouble is turned round

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
I is the Roman numeral one, single
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Problems arise when an unmarried young man has a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; the definition is 'an affair'. 'coming up' turns AIL into LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic or sexual relationship is a common sense of the word, as is a working link.

clue.text: Sort of anguished, with no heart for prayer

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them
with no heart drops H, the card-game abbreviation for hearts, rather than the word's middle letter

explanation.surface: A tormented, heartless sort says a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' is not the middle letter of the word here: it is H, as for hearts in a card game, removed before the rest is rearranged into the Latin prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamb of God is a Latin invocation in the Mass.

clue.text: Qualifier raved about bad start

indicators.note: about means around, in a different order, so the letters of raved are rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A competitor who has qualified rants about a poor opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qualifier' is the grammar sense: a word modifying a verb, adjective or another adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like quickly modify verbs, qualifying their meaning in grammar.
